label: row_0
context: This table shows that π-accepting α-substituents (carbonyl, nitrile, sulfonyl) greatly accelerate SN2 at the α-carbon. Conjugation between the adjacent π system and the C–X σ* orbital lowers the LUMO and allows developing negative charge in the transition state to delocalize. As a result, α-halo carbonyls (phenacyl chloride, chloroacetone) react 10³–10⁵ times faster than unactivated alkyl chlorides, with nitriles and esters strongly activating and sulfones modestly so.
